public.title: Undoable Database
public.description: input {initial,operations}; users are {id,name}, with distinct integer IDs, kept in creation order. Operations: create {user} (new ID), update {id,changes:{name}} (existing ID), delete {id} (existing ID), undo and redo. Every CRUD operation creates one checkpoint and clears redo. Return complete user arrays after each operation. Boundary undo/redo is a no-op. At most 20 operations and 12 users. Supported inputs are valid for this contract. Aggregate JSON-serialized input is at most 512 UTF-8 bytes, nesting depth at most 6, arrays at most 40 items, operation/call lists at most 20 items, and individual strings at most 100 ASCII characters unless a tighter bound is stated. Integers have absolute value at most 1000; output arithmetic stays within safe integers. String object keys and string path segments are nonempty safe alphanumeric/underscore names excluding __proto__, constructor and prototype. Empty arrays/objects are allowed where consistent with the contract. Output ordering follows the rules above. These bounds include all nested payloads and all operations together.
hints: Separate the documented JSON representation from the behavior being modeled.
Preserve ordering and distinguish missing values, null, zero and false carefully.

explanation: Maintain snapshots around CRUD operations and transfer snapshots between undo/redo stacks. O(q times maximum user-state size) time and storage. Functional tests check the documented adapter behavior; they do not enforce implementation technique or prohibit built-in APIs.
